title: Parameter at the intersection of two lines
source: Theory P23-9.5 Quick check 1; equate components and solve two of them
stem: The lines \(l\): \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(m\): \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{b1|int}\\{b2|int}\\{b3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) intersect. Find the value of \(\lambda\) at the point of intersection.

steps.name: K
steps.text_tex: Equate the \(x\)- and \(y\)-components: \({a1|int}+{d1|int}\lambda={b1|int}+({f1|int})\mu\) and \({a2|int}+({d2|int})\lambda={b2|int}+{f2|int}\mu\); solving gives \(\mu={M|int}\)
steps.note: Two component equations, solved simultaneously.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Solve and check the third component.

contexts.note: Includes the original lines meeting at lambda = 2, mu = 1, point (3, 0, 4)

contexts.stem: Lines \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{b1|int}\\{b2|int}\\{b3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) meet at a point \(P\). Find the value of \(\lambda\) at \(P\).

Given that the lines \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{b1|int}\\{b2|int}\\{b3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) intersect, find \(\lambda\) at their point of intersection.

title: Coordinate of the point of intersection
source: Theory P23-9.5 Quick check 2; substitute lambda back into l
stem: The lines \(l\): \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(m\): \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{b1|int}\\{b2|int}\\{b3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) intersect at the point \(P\). Find the \(z\)-coordinate of \(P\).

steps.name: K
steps.text_tex: Solving the \(x\)- and \(y\)-component equations gives \(\lambda={L|int}\) and \(\mu={M|int}\)
steps.note: Equate components and solve simultaneously.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Substitute into l (check with m).

contexts.note: Includes the original lines meeting at (3, 0, 4), z = 4

contexts.stem: Find the \(z\)-coordinate of the point where the lines \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{b1|int}\\{b2|int}\\{b3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) meet.

The lines \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{b1|int}\\{b2|int}\\{b3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) have a common point. Find its \(z\)-coordinate.

title: Cosine of the acute angle between two lines
source: Theory P23-9.5 Quick check 3; use the direction vectors and the modulus of the scalar product
stem: Find the cosine of the acute angle between the lines \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\\{a1|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\).

steps.name: K
steps.text_tex: Direction vectors: scalar product \({D|int}\), product of magnitudes \(\sqrt{{P|int}}\)
steps.note: Use the direction vectors only.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Take the modulus for the acute angle.

contexts.note: Includes the original directions (1, 2, 2) and (0, 3, 4), cos = 14/15 = 0.933

contexts.stem: The acute angle between the lines \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a1|int}\\{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}{a2|int}\\{a3|int}\\{a1|int}\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) is \(\theta\). Find \(\cos\theta\).

Two lines have direction vectors \(\begin{pmatrix}{d1|int}\\{d2|int}\\{d3|int}\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\begin{pmatrix}{f1|int}\\{f2|int}\\{f3|int}\end{pmatrix}\). Find the cosine of the acute angle between the lines.

title: Non-intersecting lines and the foot of a perpendicular

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The points \(A\) and \(B\) have position vectors \(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k}\) and \(2\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}\) respectively. The line \(l\) has equation \(\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}+\mu(2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}+4\mathbf{k})\).

(a) Show that \(l\) does not intersect the line passing through \(A\) and \(B\). [5]

(b) Find the position vector of the foot of the perpendicular from \(A\) to \(l\). [4]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: M1, carry out a correct method for finding a vector equation for AB.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: A1 OE, e.g. r = 2i − j + k + λ(i − 3j + 3k).

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: M1, equate two pairs of components of general points on their AB and l and evaluate λ or μ.

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: A1, correct value from two correct component equations.

steps.name: s5
steps.text_tex: (a) \(i\): \(1+\lambda=0\) but \(1+2\mu=-3\); \(0\ne-3\), so the lines do not intersect.
steps.note: Official MS: A1, verify that all three equations are not satisfied and the lines fail to intersect (≠ is sufficient justification, e.g. 0 ≠ −3). Conclusion needs to follow correct values.

steps.name: s6
steps.note: Official MS: B1, AP for a general point P on l, or equivalent.

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: M1, scalar product of their AP and a direction vector for l equated to zero (M0 if using OP or a parallel line through A).

steps.name: s8
steps.note: Official MS: A1.

steps.name: s9
steps.note: Official MS: A1; accept coordinates.

title: Parallel, intersecting or skew

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The line \(l\) has equation \(\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}-3\mathbf{k}+\lambda(-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k})\). The points \(A\) and \(B\) have position vectors \(-2\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}\) and \(3\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}\) respectively.

(a) Find a unit vector in the direction of \(l\). [2]

The line \(m\) passes through the points \(A\) and \(B\).

(b) Find a vector equation for \(m\). [2]

(c) Determine whether lines \(l\) and \(m\) are parallel, intersect or are skew. [5]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: M1, correct process for the modulus of the direction vector of l.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: A1 OE.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: M1, correct method to form an equation for m.

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: A1 OE, e.g. r = 3i − j + k + μ(−5i + 3j − 2k); must have r = …

steps.name: s5
steps.text_tex: (c) \((-5, 3, -2)\) is not a multiple of \((-1, 1, 2)\), so the lines are not parallel.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, justify the lines are not parallel.

steps.name: s6
steps.note: Official MS: B1, express l or m in component form.

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: M1, equate two pairs of components and solve simultaneously for λ or μ.

steps.name: s8
steps.note: Official MS: A1, correct λ or μ.

steps.name: s9
steps.text_tex: (c) \(k\): \(-3+11=8\) but \(-1-1=-2\); \(8\ne-2\), so the lines do not intersect and are skew.
steps.note: Official MS: A1, all three equations not satisfied, conclude skew; dependent on the 4 previous marks.
